notes:
Lead summary: inbound signup (self-serve) from marketing page; trial credit used. Currently small support SaaS; want AI answers inside agent UI. Primary pain: perceived latency in Europe and intermittent spikes for US-West users. Cost-sensitive; want hosted API, no private deployment now.

Recent timeline (short):
- 2026-02-18: intro call (Jordan + Maya) - product fit looks good, demo of hosted API. FF: ff_20260218_aspenshore_initial_call.
- 2026-02-22: follow-up email with quickstart + sample integration snippets (thread-ax12345).
- 2026-03-02: latency deep-dive call w/ engineering; shared p95 numbers, grab logs. FF: ff_20260302_latency_deepdive.
- 2026-03-05: POC requested — 7-day run vs two regions (us-east-1 and eu-west-1). Jira RED-4123 opened for instrumentation.

Customer environment / constraints:
- Frontend is SPA with US and EU customers; EU office reports 800-1200ms perceived reply time on chat flows, backend logs show token-level latency spikes up to 1.5s for some requests.
- Using single region (us-west-2) default; wants guidance on region choice and routing.
- Authentication via SSO (SAML) for internal admin console — wants audit logs and SOC2 proof.

Workload & targets:
- Workloads: chat-first support assistant (multi-turn), doc search + RAG for KB, short summarization for ticket notes.
- Latency target: p95 < 600ms for chat responses (perceived streaming), p50 < 200ms ideally.
- Throughput: modest (burst to 30 req/s), typical steady < 5 req/s.
- Cost sensitivity: low-to-medium; will optimize if latency gains small.

Observed issues and hypotheses:
- Region mismatch: EU users routed to us-west-2 causing RTT spikes.
- Timeouts: frontend uses 8s client timeout; occasional 10s server ops cause retries and duplicate prompts.
- Prompt engineering: long conversation history retained on every call (avg 3.6k tokens) causing increased model decode time.
- No caching for top-K FAQ responses; repeated identical prompts create unnecessary load.

Recommended perf tuning (advice provided during call):
- Region choice / routing: run POC with us-east-1 (good midwest) + eu-west-1. Suggest edge routing for EU office -> eu-west-1. Add health-based routing rule for <700ms target.
- Timeouts & retries: set client-side timeout to 12s for non-streaming but prefer streaming responses to reduce perceived latency; backoff retries disabled for idempotency on chat message endpoints.
- Prompt length guidance: limit history tokens to 1200 tokens; summarize older turns server-side into short memories (200-300 tokens) before sending. Use system messages + minimal context for retrieval calls.
- Caching: implement prefix/KV caching for repeated Q/A and common KB retrievals. Cache embedding similarity results for 24h for stable KB.
- Batching / concurrency: enable small continuous batching on server (2-4 reqs) for throughput at peak but cap batch delay to 15ms to avoid audible latency.
- Model selection: recommend mid-sized model variant for chat (lower decode time) during peak; fall back to larger model for complex summarization.
- Observability: instrument p50/p95 token latency, cold-start times, routing breakdown by region, cost per 1M tokens. Use Redwood Console route dashboards.

Quotes / snippets: "EU feels slow — sometimes chat takes >1s and agents complain". "If we can get p95 under 600ms we'll roll this product to entire customer base."

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood to provision trial endpoints in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (SE: Maya) and supply curl + SDK snippets (actioned 2026-03-09).
- AspenShore engs to run 7-day POC, collect p95/p50, attach logs to RED-4178.
- Follow up call scheduled 2026-03-16 to review POC metrics and finalize timeouts and prompt truncation strategy.

Blockers / risks:
- SSO config may affect routing if admin control plane locked down; needs security team sign-off.
- EU latency may be due to customer's VPN; need to rule out network layer before attributing to model placement.

Internal notes for AE/SE:
- Keep emphasis on hosted_api good for self-serve -> low friction onboarding.
- Prepare short checklist for customer engineers: 1) region test, 2) enable streaming, 3) cap history, 4) enable KV cache.
- Attach drive docs: https://drive.redwood/aspenshore/pricing-deck-v2 and security faq link.

Useful metrics to capture in POC: ["p50_latency_ms","p95_latency_ms","avg_tokens_per_response","cold_start_ms","requests_per_second","cost_per_1M_tokens"].

Sales hints: close window likely Apr 2026 if POC good. Upsell path: Dedicated later when volume grows or EU residency required.
